subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: What trusted-plugin and recovery contract should govern a synchronous veto immediately before OpenClaw persists configuration changes?
rationale: The repository already has the correct internal commit seam, but source evidence cannot decide which plugins may block writes, which sensitive fields they receive, how timeouts and hook errors behave, or how operators recover when a validator itself blocks repair.

options.title: Trusted synchronous veto
options.body: Expose a typed hook for explicitly trusted code plugins, composed after built-in validation and SecretRef preflight with bounded execution, redacted context, and an operator recovery bypass.

options.title: Core validators only
options.body: Keep the final veto internal to core and offer plugins only non-blocking post-validation observation, avoiding third-party denial-of-service authority.

options.title: Unified persistence contract
options.body: Fold config writes into the broader durable-state hook design at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48509 before adding any config-specific public API.

recommendation.title: Trusted synchronous veto
recommendation.body: Expose a typed hook for explicitly trusted code plugins, composed after built-in validation and SecretRef preflight with bounded execution, redacted context, and an operator recovery bypass.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest combined history on the shared config writer, gateway config flow, blocking hooks, and the issue's recent product review.
